feature: TLS HTTP/2 and WebTransport HTTP/2 through SOCKS5 CONNECT

scope.http2: standalone http2.socks5_runtime Client with relative, absolute, and unbounded TLS host connection entry points
scope.webtransport: direct EndpointClient setup and ReconnectingEndpointClient tls_socks5_proxy target
scope.dns: the origin hostname remains a SOCKS5 domain address and is not resolved locally
scope.deadline: one awake-clock timestamp spans proxy DNS/TCP, SOCKS negotiation, CONNECT, origin TLS/h2 ALPN, HTTP/2 bootstrap, and endpoint admission
scope.identity: origin hostname remains the TLS certificate and SNI identity and the HTTP/2 or WebTransport authority
scope.error_boundary: SOCKS protocol and reply errors remain in http2.socks5_runtime and do not widen core HTTP/2 Connection state

reference.implementation: independent Python socket peer plus existing Netz RFC 1928 codec
reference.oracle_boundary: the Python peer parses the greeting and domain-form CONNECT request independently, relays opaque TLS bytes, and serves the minimal HTTP/2 origin

implementation.adoption: runtime.Client.adoptTlsStream transfers a caller-connected TCP stream into origin-authenticated TLS and HTTP/2 while copying authority ownership
implementation.composition: http2.socks5_runtime validates and allocates origin identity before proxy I/O, opens SOCKS CONNECT, and transfers the stream to the runtime adopter
implementation.reconnect: the WebTransport target opens a fresh SOCKS, TLS, HTTP/2, and Session generation after transport loss and rejects the old handle
implementation.test_structure: HTTP CONNECT and SOCKS5 two-generation scenarios share a dedicated proxy_tests module instead of enlarging the general reconnect test file

native_cases: timeout and authority allocation rejection before proxy I/O
SOCKS greeting selects no-auth and CONNECT uses address type domain for localhost
exact destination port and success reply before TLS bytes
TLS 1.3 certificate verification and mandatory h2 ALPN
WebTransport Session and DATAGRAM on generation one
transport close makes the first handle stale
generation two opens another SOCKS tunnel and completes a new Session
